key_insight: Diagnostic accuracy alone can hide whether a medical LLM used patient evidence correctly, so the paper audits evidence use rather than just final answers.
clinical_relevance: This matters because clinically plausible differential reasoning can look like failure, while shortcut-like reasoning may be missed unless evidence interactions are checked.
method: Decomposed each case into evidence units and scored diagnoses under controlled subsets of evidence.
Mined low-order interactions in diagnostic margins to find support, conflict, and cancellation effects.
Separated interaction discovery from failure assignment, then used robustness checks and clinical review for suspicious cases.
evidence_signal: Across five open-weight LLMs on DDXPlus, CupCase, and MedCase, most interaction strength came from faithful support and differential conflict or cancellation, with a blinded 130-item reviewer sample highlighting invalid or shortcut-like cases mainly in negated/absent findings and local evidence.
watch_item: Because evidence interactions are diagnosis-relative, some large or negative effects may be clinically reasonable differentials rather than model failures, so interpretation needs expert review.
paper_title: Auditing Evidence Use in Medical LLM Diagnosis
